correctness.rationale: The counted measure is unambiguously the pushforward of rooted spanning forests, with root multiplicity. Chebotarev–Shamis weighted determinant is valid for negative weights. The right-vertex diagonal entries 3,1,1,-1 are nonzero, and the 2x2 Schur complement directly gives the claimed formula. Modulo-two reduction of every sign proves all even widths nonsingular. A concrete odd-width sign assignment has zero Schur determinant. At degrees one and two the three support cases reduce to polynomials with exactly the claimed integer roots, including the unique width-five 20-frequency exception. An independent root census plus integer FWHT checks all 1364 frequencies n=1..5; infinity proof is symbolic.

The closest published complete K2n Fourier analysis concerns the different spanning-tree indicator, which is sparse and not the rooted-forest counting measure. Searches for aliases and stronger formulations found no decisive coverage. The possibility of an unindexed previously evaluated specialization remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The canonical root-weighted forest ensemble has a natural edge-incidence Fourier counting measure. The explicit all-width signed spectrum and parity invertibility classification reveal which full signals are recoverable, while the unique degree-two resonance at n=5 separates global singularity from recoverability of low-order features. The result is a motivated exact structural classification and finite low-degree boundary, not a gratuitous small numerical table.
